title: Linux.Mirai_Incident_Response_47f
description: Investigate and respond to a potential Linux.Mirai trojan infection on a victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected outbound network connections and elevated CPU usage. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident involving the Linux.Mirai trojan.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for unauthorized or suspicious services that may indicate trojan activity.
levels.solution: Check running services and their associated processes for anything unusual or unexpected. The service name associated with the trojan's persistence mechanism is `network-diagnostics.timer`. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to investigate.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their associated processes for anything unusual or unexpected.

levels.title: Identify Scheduled Tasks
levels.content: Determine if any scheduled tasks or timers are responsible for automatically executing the malware on the victim host.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services that may be triggering malicious activity. The name of the timer or task responsible for executing the trojan's components is `network-diagnostics.timer`. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to investigate.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services that may be triggering malicious activity.

levels.title: Identify Reverse Shell Component
levels.content: Identify the component responsible for providing unauthorized remote shell access to the victim host.
levels.solution: Look for scripts or processes that establish connections to external hosts on unusual ports. The script name or process responsible for maintaining reverse shell access is `/usr/local/lib/.netd/revshell.sh`. Use the command `ps aux | grep revshell` to investigate.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for scripts or processes that establish connections to external hosts on unusual ports.
